evidence.activity: Refreshed airport lounges to include interior design elements from local artists and students

evidence.section: Annual report > Infrastructure Investments > Passenger-facing infrastructure

evidence.activity: Culinary and product innovation teams and chefs develop menus for inflight and food services
evidence.quote: Our culinary and product innovation teams translate menu concepts into meals that can be produced consistently across markets, while our community of chefs across the network brings cultural depth and diversity to the offering.
evidence.section: Annual report > Synergistic Growth Through Non-Aviation

creativity.criterion: level 1: menu design as a routine business input

evidence.activity: SATS Foundation funds registered charity programmes in Singapore, mainly food security

evidence.activity: Employee volunteering through SATS Foundation programmes
evidence.quote: Employee volunteerism remained strong, with approximately 900 volunteer hours recorded in FY2026, of which 76% supported food security programmes, followed by initiatives benefitting the elderly and youth.
evidence.section: Annual report > Caring for Our Communities > Caring for Community

evidence.activity: AISATS Morning Nutrition Programme providing daily nutrition to rural government school children
evidence.quote: The Morning Nutrition Programme reached 35,000 government school children across rural Karnataka with daily fortified nutrition and milk, improving attendance and classroom engagement.
evidence.section: Annual report > Caring for Our Communities > India

community.criterion: level 3: named programme with participant numbers

evidence.activity: AISATS Family Strengthening programmes for vulnerable children
evidence.quote: Family Strengthening programmes supported 202 vulnerable children across Alibaug, Hyderabad and Bengaluru through integrated interventions covering health, nutrition and livelihood stability.
evidence.section: Annual report > Caring for Our Communities > India

community.criterion: level 2-3: named programme with participant numbers

evidence.activity: AISATS support for girls to continue primary education
evidence.quote: In India, AISATS supported 80 girls in higher primary education, providing resources to reduce dropout rates and encourage continued schooling.
evidence.section: Annual report > Caring for Our Communities > India

community.criterion: level 2: external education support, limited reach

evidence.activity: AISATS support for children with disabilities through therapy, assistive devices and caregiver training
evidence.quote: The organisation also extended support to 90 children with hearing, sight and other disabilities, enabling access to therapy, assistive devices and specialised caregiver training to promote independence and inclusion.
evidence.section: Annual report > Caring for Our Communities > India

cross_cultural.criterion: level 2: specific programme removing barriers for people with disabilities, limited reach

evidence.activity: Youth Outreach Programme with Singapore Airlines introducing students to aviation careers
evidence.quote: Through a collaboration with Singapore Airlines, we co-organised a Youth Outreach Programme conducted twice annually, introducing students to the aviation ecosystem and exposing them to career pathways across ground handling, food solutions and airport operations.
evidence.section: Annual report > Caring for Our Communities > Youth Outreach Programme

community.criterion: level 3: named external education programme with participant numbers

evidence.activity: Scholarships and financial assistance for students through partnerships with educational institutions
evidence.quote: We also partnered with three educational institutions to provide scholarships and financial assistance to students pursuing their academic goals.
evidence.section: Annual report > Caring for Our Communities > Empowering Community

evidence.activity: SATS Foundation Education Awards bursaries for employees' children and young people
evidence.quote: The SATS Foundation Education Awards honour the dedication of our employees by supporting the aspirations of their children and young people across our community.
evidence.section: Annual report > Caring for Our Communities, Empowering Futures

community.criterion: level 2: named bursary programme, no figures

evidence.activity: AISATS water purification systems improving safe drinking water access in remote areas of India
evidence.quote: AISATS partnered with cross-sector partners on an initiative in India to deploy advanced water purification systems at Indian Army forward locations, improving access to safe drinking water for personnel and communities in some of the country’s most remote and demanding operating conditions.
evidence.section: Annual report > Caring for Our Communities > India

community.criterion: level 2: specific community initiative, no figures

evidence.activity: Built to Lead flagship leadership programme for people managers
evidence.quote: Our flagship programme, Built to Lead (BTL), serves as the foundational leadership programme for people managers.
evidence.section: Annual report > Corporate Governance Report > Leadership development

evidence.activity: ELEVATE global mobility programme of short-term international assignments for high-potential staff
evidence.quote: Under ELEVATE, selected high-potential employees undertake short-term international assignments with specific business projects and objectives.
evidence.section: Annual report > Corporate Governance Report > Leadership development

evidence.quote: In FY2026, we launched a group-wide Workplace Inclusion eLearning programme to establish a common baseline of inclusive practices, achieving a 95% completion rate across our global workforce.
evidence.section: Annual report > People > Building a Global Culture as OneSATS

cross_cultural.criterion: level 2: specific current inclusion practice across the workforce

evidence.activity: SATS Network of WoMen, a regional employee network piloted in selected EMEA markets
evidence.quote: In EMEA, we also introduced the SATS Network of WoMen, a regional initiative across all genders to foster personal empowerment, professional development and community building.
evidence.section: Annual report > People > Building a Global Culture as OneSATS

cross_cultural.criterion: level 2: employee network, regional pilot with limited membership

evidence.quote: Seven out of 10 Directors (70%) are of Asian ethnicity, while three Directors (30%) are of Caucasian descent.
evidence.section: Annual report > Corporate Governance Report > Board Diversity Targets, Timelines and Progress > Ethnicity

evidence.activity: SG Hub innovation centre trialling autonomous vehicles and new operating concepts
evidence.quote: SG Hub serves as our innovation and system design centre, where new operating concepts are validated in live operations before scaling across the network.

creativity.reason: Level 1: creative work appears only as a routine input, such as menu development and lounge interior design (the lounge item is still planned), in an aviation services and catering business.

community.reason: Level 3: external education and community investment with substantial reach shown by indicators, including 35,000 school children fed, more than 22 IPC programmes, over 300 students per year in youth outreach, and about 900 volunteer hours, though not central to strategy.

cross_cultural.reason: Level 2: specific current activities with limited reach, namely a group-wide inclusion eLearning, a regional employee network pilot with 120 members, and disability support for 90 children; board ethnicity data is demographics only.

entrepreneurship.reason: Level 1: only the company's own innovation is described, with no service or programme that enables founders or small businesses.

ai.notes: Several community programmes (E5-E8, E12) are run by AISATS, an Indian joint venture, which the report presents as part of SATS's community work. The SATS Network of WoMen is described as 'piloted in selected EMEA markets' (page 24) and as a regional initiative with 120 inaugural members; a Group-wide rollout is only planned. Cross-cultural was torn between levels 2 and 3 and set to the lower level under the tie-break rule. The 1,800 families helped after the Hong Kong fire appear only in a stats call-out with no full sentence to quote, so no record was created. The board missed its 35% female representation target (30% actual). The report refers to a separate Sustainability Report 2026 and ESG Databook for more metrics, but coverage is sufficient on every theme without them.
